Theorem
[Properties of Fourier transform] ↗ def:fourier-transform-l2 ↗ thm:plancherel-theorem 1. ch4:4.3.1-thm-2\group Fourier Transform

For $u,v\in L^2(\R ^n)$, \[ \int u\bar v\, dx=\int \hat u\, \overline{\hat v}\, dy, \quad \widehat{D^\alpha u}=(iy)^\alpha \hat u, \quad (u*v)^\wedge =(2\pi )^{n/2}\hat u\hat v, \quad u=(\hat u)^\vee , \] whenever the indicated derivatives lie in $L^2$.

Proof

\sketch Polarization of Plancherel gives the inner-product formula. Integration by parts proves the derivative rule for smooth compactly supported functions and density extends it. Fubini gives convolution; Gaussian approximate identities give Fourier inversion almost everywhere.

□
